reference_title: California Trenching and Shoring Manual (Caltrans, June 2011, Revision 2 - July 2025)

sections.title: Lateral Earth Pressures for Restrained Shoring Systems
sections.summary: An anchored/braced wall of exposed height H with embedded depth D uses a TRAPEZOIDAL apparent earth pressure (AEP) distribution, not the triangular distribution used for cantilevers, because the support points restrain the wall (Figure 8-1). Anchored walls are used when the height is impractical for a cantilever or the cantilever displacement would be too large for adjacent structures/utilities.
sections.body: An anchored wall of exposed height H over which soil is retained, with embedded depth D, includes structural supports (braced) or ground anchors (Figure 8-1). An anchored wall is used when the restrained height is too large for a practical cantilever, or when the estimated lateral displacement of a cantilever is too large given existing structures or utilities behind the wall. The lateral earth pressure increases with depth and a triangular pressure is used for cantilevers; for braced or ground-anchor walls a trapezoidal-shaped apparent earth pressure distribution needs to be developed instead.
key_points: Restrained (braced/anchored) walls use a TRAPEZOIDAL apparent earth pressure, not triangular
Wall of exposed height H, embedded depth D, with braces or ground anchors
Used when a cantilever is impractical (height) or its displacement is too large
Figure 8-1 shows the anchored/braced wall pressure

sections.title: Cohesionless Soils - Trapezoidal Apparent Earth Pressure
sections.summary: For braced/anchored walls in cohesionless soil, Figure 8-2 (single level) and Figure 8-3 (multiple levels) may be used. Single level: sigma_a = f x P/((2/3)H) = 1.3 x P/((2/3)H) (Eq. 8-2-1), with the triangular resultant P = (1/2)gamma H^2 Ka (Eq. 8-2-2) and the trapezoidal resultant PT = 0.65[gamma H^2 Ka] (Eq. 8-2-3), so f = 1.3 (Eq. 8-2-4) and PT = 1.3P (Eq. 8-2-5). Multiple levels: sigma_a = 1.3P/[H - (1/3)(H1 + Hn+1)] (Eq. 8-2-6), H1 from the ground surface to the uppermost anchor level, Hn+1 from the grade at the bottom of the wall to the lowermost.
sections.body: The lateral earth pressure distribution for braced/anchored walls in cohesionless soils may be determined using Figure 8-2 (single level) and Figure 8-3 (multi-level). For walls with a single level of anchors or braces the maximum ordinate is sigma_a = f x P/((2/3)H) = 1.3 x P/((2/3)H) (Eq. 8-2-1). The factor f is a constant that converts a triangular pressure distribution to a trapezoidal one; the triangular distributions are not shown in Figures 8-2 and 8-3 but are used to calculate the resultants. The resultant for the triangular distribution is P = ((1/2)gamma)(H^2)(Ka) (Eq. 8-2-2); for the trapezoidal distribution PT = 0.65[gamma(H^2)(Ka)] (Eq. 8-2-3). Setting PT = [(1/2)gamma(H^2)(Ka)]f = 0.65[gamma(H^2)(Ka)] gives f = 1.3 (Eq. 8-2-4), therefore PT = 1.3P (Eq. 8-2-5). For the multilevel anchored wall (Figure 8-3), the maximum ordinate is sigma_a = 1.3P / [H - (1/3)(H1 + Hn+1)] (Eq. 8-2-6), where H1 is the distance from the ground surface to the uppermost anchor level and Hn+1 is the distance from the grade at the bottom of the wall to the lowermost anchor level.
key_points: Trapezoidal resultant PT = 1.3 * triangular resultant P (Eq. 8-2-5)
Single level: sigma_a = 1.3 x P/((2/3)H) (Eq. 8-2-1); triangular resultant P = (1/2)gamma H^2 Ka (Eq. 8-2-2)
Multi-level max ordinate sigma_a = 1.3P/[H - (1/3)(H1 + Hn+1)] (Eq. 8-2-6)
H1 = surface to uppermost anchor; Hn+1 = wall base to lowermost anchor
Single-level pressure from Figure 8-2; multi-level from Figure 8-3

equations.description: Trapezoidal AEP resultant PT = 1.3 * triangular resultant P.
Multi-level cohesionless AEP maximum ordinate sigma_a = 1.3P/[H - (1/3)(H1 + Hn+1)].

sections.title: Cohesive Soils - AEP by Stability Number
sections.summary: The cohesive AEP is related to the stability number Ns = gamma*H/cu (Eq. 8-3-1), cu the average undrained shear strength (= unconfined compressive strength / 2 when the undrained phi = 0). Stiff to hard (Ns <= 4): sigma_a = 0.2(gamma)(H) to 0.4(gamma)(H) (Eq. 8-3-2), the factor by engineering judgment. Soft to medium stiff (Ns >= 6): sigma_a = Ka gamma H (Eq. 8-3-3), Ka = 1 - 4cu1/(gamma H) + 2 sqrt(2) (D/H)[1 - 5.14cu2/(gamma H)] >= 0.25 (Eq. 8-3-4, FHWA; for a weaker lower clay layer). For 4 < Ns < 6 use the larger. Figure 8-4 gives the diagram.
sections.body: The lateral earth pressure distribution for cohesive soils is related to the stability number Ns = gamma*H/cu (Eq. 8-3-1), where gamma is the total unit weight of soil, H the wall height, and cu the average undrained shear strength (average undrained cohesion) of the soil; the undrained cohesion is equal to the unconfined compressive strength divided by 2, which is true when the undrained angle of internal friction phi is zero (note, p. 8-5). Stiff to hard (8-3.01): for braced or anchored walls with Ns less than or equal to 4, the lateral earth pressure may be determined using Figure 8-4 with maximum ordinate sigma_a = 0.2(gamma)(H) to 0.4(gamma)(H) (Eq. 8-3-2). The stability number is dimensionless; a higher Ns means a higher shear strength is required to maintain stability, so the in-situ field condition needs to be determined and best engineering judgment is needed to use the applicable factor between 0.2 and 0.4. Soft to medium stiff (8-3.02): with Ns equal to or larger than 6, sigma_a = Ka*gamma*H (Eq. 8-3-3) (Figure 8-4). For 4 < Ns < 6, use the larger sigma_a from Eqs. 8-3-2 and 8-3-3. Ka may be determined using Eq. 8-3-4 per FHWA and is not to be less than 0.25: Ka = 1 - 4(cu1)/((gamma)(H)) + 2*sqrt(2)*(D/H)*[1 - 5.14(cu2)/((gamma)(H))] >= 0.25, where cu1 = undrained shear strength of the retained soil above the excavation line (upper cohesive layer), cu2 = undrained shear strength below the excavation line (lower layer), gamma = total unit weight of retained soil, H = wall height, D = depth from the grade in front of the wall to the potential failure surface below. Eq. 8-3-4 addresses an excavation in an upper cohesive layer over a lower cohesive layer whose undrained shear strength is significantly less; the results may be unexpected when the lower strength is approximately 80 percent or more of the upper, and although Ka from Eq. 8-3-4 can be negative, the equation gives reasonable results when the lower soil is significantly weaker than the upper.
key_points: Stability number Ns = gamma*H/cu (Eq. 8-3-1); cu = unconfined compressive strength / 2
Stiff-hard clay (Ns <= 4): sigma_a = 0.2 to 0.4 * gamma * H (Eq. 8-3-2)
Soft-medium clay (Ns >= 6): sigma_a = Ka * gamma * H (Eq. 8-3-3)
Ka = 1 - 4cu1/(gamma H) + 2 sqrt(2)(D/H)[1 - 5.14cu2/(gamma H)], not less than 0.25 (Eq. 8-3-4, FHWA)
4 < Ns < 6: use the larger sigma_a of the two envelopes
Eq. 8-3-4 is for a lower clay layer much weaker than the upper; results may be unexpected when cu2 is about 80% or more of cu1
Section 10-3: heave and slip circle failure in soft clays should be checked when No = gamma H/c exceeds 6

equations.description: Stiff-hard cohesive AEP max ordinate sigma_a = 0.2 to 0.4 * gamma * H (Ns <= 4).
Soft-medium cohesive AEP max ordinate sigma_a = Ka * gamma * H (Ns >= 6).

FHWA coefficient for soft to medium stiff cohesive AEP: Ka = 1 - 4(cu1)/((gamma)(H)) + 2 sqrt(2) (D/H)[1 - 5.14(cu2)/((gamma)(H))] >= 0.25 (cu1 above, cu2 below the excavation line; D to the potential failure surface).

sections.title: Calculation Procedures (Single and Multiple Anchor; Embedment FS)
sections.summary: Single anchor: convert active pressure above the excavation to a trapezoid, take moments about the anchor for embedment D with FS = 1.3, then with FS = 1.0 to back-calculate the anchor load T, and finish with max shear/moment. Multiple anchors: use the Hinge Method (force AND moment equilibrium, shear/moment = 0 at the tip) or the Tributary Area Method; embedment D uses FS = 1.3 for external stability. Point of fixity is 0.25D to 0.8D below the excavation.
sections.body: Single ground anchor/brace procedure: (1) determine the earth pressure coefficients (classical theories, Chapter 4); (2) convert the active pressure above the excavation line to a trapezoid; (3) take moments about the anchor to calculate embedment depth D using a factor of safety of 1.3; (4) take moments about the anchor with FS = 1.0 to calculate the ground-anchor load T in the next step; (5) set the horizontal force summation to zero to find the anchor force T; (6) calculate maximum bending moment and shear to size the vertical member and lagging. Multiple anchors: per FHWA the two methods are the Hinge Method and the Tributary Area Method. The Tributary Area Method balances only force summation (large tip moment); the Hinge Method satisfies force AND moment equilibrium so shear and moment equal zero at the tip. Embedment D for multiple anchors is found by taking moments about the last anchor using FS = 1.3 for external stability. Deflection: support deflections are taken as zero (like a simple beam); the point of fixity varies from 0.25D to 0.8D below the excavation level depending on effective pile diameter and soil type.
key_points: Embedment depth D: take moments about the anchor with FS = 1.3 (external stability)
Anchor/brace load T: take moments with FS = 1.0, then sum horizontal forces
Multiple anchors: Hinge Method (force + moment equilibrium) or Tributary Area Method
Hinge Method sets shear and moment to zero at the pile tip
Point of fixity 0.25D to 0.8D below the excavation level
